subject: Galileo ISV integration - takeover triage playbook and SLA handoff
messages:
From: Ava Martinez <ava@galileo-sys.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Integration failure patterns during peak bursts (Galileo)

Hi Priyom / Marissa,

We surfaced a high-severity pattern this morning: multiple customers connected via our Galileo connector hit high tail-latency when Redwood model routing falls back to the small-quantized variant. The failure window correlates with our nightly bulk job (02:00 UTC) and a spike in simultaneous batch requests from two ISV customers. Attached are the logs and a short trace.

We need a coordinated triage and an SLA handoff plan — our CTO is asking for an escalation path so we can provide committed response times to our customers while Redwood stabilizes routing behavior. Can someone on your side drive a short-term mitigation and a mid-term runbook we can include in our partner portal?

What we need now:
- Confirmation of whether fallback routing can be prevented for specific Galileo API keys (per-tenant bypass)
- A conservative routing policy we can document (e.g., pin to larger model family during batch windows)
- A contact list and an expected response SLA for Sev-1 incidents that involve cross-system fallbacks

We can be available for a 30-min quick triage today at 16:00 ET if that helps.

Thanks,
Ava
Ops Lead, Galileo Systems

Attachments: galileo_error_logs.zip, supplemental_trace.txt

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>

Marissa / Jonas — forwarding Galileo's note. Initial read: looks like routing fallback + concurrent batching edge case. I want to propose a short-term "takeover" plan to ensure their impacted tenants are pinned to the higher-throughput model family until we fix the routing heuristics.

Action items I suggest we split:
- Jonas: validate fallback triggers and whether per-API-key routing overrides exist (infra/runtime)
- Marissa: own partner communication and a temporary SLA note for Galileo customers (48-hour committed response, and a 4-hour mitigation window for Sev-1)
- Vanessa: coordinate CS outreach and update the partner portal doc once we have wording

I'll join the triage at 16:00 ET. If Jonas can't implement per-key overrides quickly, we should prepare a plan B: rate-limit or window isolation for the Galileo API keys while we roll a runtime fix.

Priyom
Principal Partner Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Quick update from runtime: the fallback decision is triggered when the service observes sustained queue growth (+KV cache pressure) and the model family for the request is flagged as "fallback-allowed" in the routing policy. There is an experimental per-tenant override flag in our config service but it is gated behind a safe-mode rollout. I can flip it for Galileo's test key but will require a controlled rollout:

Planned short-term steps (hours):
1) Flip per-tenant override to pin Galileo test key to the larger model family (non-quantized) — deploy within 60-90 mins for a single key (manual guardrails).
2) Introduce request-level logging hooks so we can watch queue depth for the next 12 hours.
3) If queue growth persists, apply traffic isolation (rate caps) to the affected API keys for the scheduled bulk windows.

Risk: pinning prevents cost-saving fallbacks and may increase token compute costs. We'll need Galileo sign-off.

I'll start the override on the test key once Marissa confirms partner messaging and we have a time window.

— Jonas
Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Ava Martinez <ava@galileo-sys.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Galileo ISV integration - takeover triage playbook and SLA handoff

Ava — thanks for flagging and for the logs. We propose the following kickoff plan:

Short-term (today, 16:00 ET triage):
- Redwood will pin Galileo's affected API keys to the larger model family for the next 24 hours (Jonas will apply per-tenant override to test key and then the production keys after quick verification).
- Redwood will provide a 4-hour mitigation window target for Sev-1 incidents involving cross-system fallbacks, and a 48-hour committed follow-up for a permanent fix (runbook + runtime change).
- Galileo to confirm which API keys/tenant IDs should be pinned; provide a list by 15:00 ET so we can stage changes.

Mid-term (next 2 weeks):
- Joint runbook (we'll draft, share for Galileo review): detection triggers, escalation contact list, rollback/playback steps, and cost-awareness notes (how pinning affects billing).
- Red-amber-green dashboard link for joint monitoring (we'll share a read-only dashboard).

We will attach the runbook draft after the triage; for now I attached our internal integration_runbook_v2.pdf as a baseline.

If that sounds OK, confirm the list of keys and we will proceed with the manual override during the triage.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Partner Manager, Redwood Inference
Attachments: integration_runbook_v2.pdf
